title: Fynaptix · Space Economy Research
heading: Space Economy Intelligence
subheading: Launch, satellites, constellations & the post-SpaceX-IPO landscape
disclaimer: Not financial advice. This page organizes public information for research purposes only — not a recommendation to buy or sell any security. Space is capital-intensive with heavy government-customer concentration. Verify current prices and do your own due diligence before investing.

kpis.label: Global space economy estimated at ~$626B in 2026; Goldman Sachs and McKinsey both project a climb to $1.8T by 2035 alongside a rising wave of sector M&A.

kpis.sub: BELOW POST-IPO HIGH · STARSHIP FLIGHT 14 LAUNCHES TODAY
kpis.label: SPCX trades around $148–149, roughly 26% below its ~$202 post-IPO high set in mid-June and still well above the $135 IPO price; Starship Flight 14 — the first true orbital attempt, carrying 26 Starlink V3 satellites — is targeted for today, Sept 28, after three prior slips.

kpis.sub: 2026 YTD SPACE STARTUP FUNDING · ALREADY A RECORD
kpis.label: Global private investment in space and satellite startups holds at $20.3B for 2026, already exceeding every full prior year with roughly three months still to go; capital is flowing through smaller, more numerous checks rather than mega-rounds.

kpis.sub: IRIDIUM STOCKHOLDERS APPROVE ROCKET LAB MERGER
kpis.label: Iridium stockholders approved the Rocket Lab acquisition on Sept 24 with 99.6% of votes cast (~81% of shares); an FCC review is next, with closing now guided to mid-2027 and Neutron's pad delivery still tracking Q4 2026.

tiers.label: Scale Players
tiers.note: Tiered by maturity/risk — not a ranked buy list.

rows.angle: Starlink connectivity revenue is up 66% YoY to a ~$17B annualized run-rate on 12M subscribers, still the only consistently profitable segment; shares trade around $148–149, up off the $135 IPO price but ~26% below the ~$202 post-IPO high set in mid-June.
rows.watch for: Starship Flight 14 — the first true orbital attempt, 26 Starlink V3 satellites, ~10-hour mission with booster and ship splashdowns — targets today, Sept 28, after slipping three times in three weeks; several insider-lockup unlock tranches remain through year-end.

rows.angle: Iridium stockholders approved the merger Sept 24 with 99.6% of votes cast (~81% of shares), clearing the last major deal-completion risk beyond a still-pending FCC review; Neutron's pad delivery remains on track for Q4 2026 with customers already reserving launch slots at $50–55M.
rows.watch for: Closing is now guided to mid-2027 — later than earlier company language — and Neutron's actual maiden flight is still exposed to slipping into 2027; Rocket Lab is guiding to a $17–23M adjusted EBITDA loss for Q3 after $1.53B of H1 2026 equity raises, and RKLB remains well off its 52-week high of $151.

rows.angle: Space and Mission Systems revenue is tracking past $13B in 2026, underpinned by a $4.7B Lockheed PAC-3 MSE propulsion award — L3Harris's largest PAC-3 propulsion contract to date — and a share of the SDA's $3.5B Tranche 3 tracking-layer awards.
rows.watch for: Shares are still hovering near 52-week lows with the Kubasik-era securities-claims investigation unresolved; new contract wins haven't moved the stock. Also sits in the Defense sleeve — don't double-count exposure.

tiers.label: Growth / Speculative
tiers.note: Tiered by maturity/risk — not a ranked buy list.

rows.angle: 13 BlueBird satellites are now in orbit on a $1.30B contracted backlog with 60+ MNO partners covering roughly 3 billion subscribers, plus a Rakuten/AST J-LEO venture valued up to $1B as the network moves toward commercial beta.
rows.watch for: Q2 revenue of $31.5M missed consensus by ~8%, weighed down by a $125.9M charge tied to the BB7 launch incident; a $1.15B convertible raise in July adds dilution risk on top of ~$610M of quarterly capex.

rows.angle: Completed the SXM-11 satellite handover and carries a record $1.8B backlog; shares extended gains (+3% Sept 24) on fresh contract wins and analyst upgrades.
rows.watch for: Net insider selling has reached roughly $259M over the past 12 months, and converting the backlog into recognized revenue remains the open question.

rows.angle: Delivered its first profitable quarter with Q2 revenue up 58% YoY, opened a new Berlin facility to scale Pelican satellite production, and rallied 5.8% on Sept 25–26 as Google's Project Suncatcher announcement lifted sentiment across pure-play space names.
rows.watch for: A co-founder sold roughly $1.8M of stock this week, and tightening SpaceX rideshare launch capacity by 2028 is a margin risk the market hasn't fully priced in; consensus price target ($32.77) sits well above the ~$17 share price but the average rating is still Hold.

rows.angle: Selected as one of 15 vendors on the Space Force's NITE STAR test-and-training IDIQ, with an award ceiling over $980M, while still carrying a record ~$542M backlog.
rows.watch for: NITE STAR is a multi-vendor IDIQ with no guaranteed revenue — task orders still have to be won separately — and a disclosed $1.15B of net insider selling over 12 months, against a roughly $1B market cap, remains unexplained.

private_watchlist.name: Blue Origin
private_watchlist.note: Traced the root cause of its most recent New Glenn anomaly to an engine issue; the next flight is targeting the booster's first-ever reuse plus a debut launch from Vandenberg Space Force Base, though no confirmed date emerged this week.

private_watchlist.name: Firefly Aerospace
private_watchlist.note: Completed a new cleanroom on Sept 22 to accelerate spacecraft production; the Alpha Block 2 rocket's debut has slipped to Q4 2026, and shares remain well below their 12-month high as the broader small-launch segment waits on SpaceX's rideshare capacity to tighten.

private_watchlist.name: Stoke Space
private_watchlist.note: No fresh update this week beyond the previously disclosed $1B Series E (total raised $2.3B, ~$10B valuation); Nova Block 2 — a 15-metric-ton fully reusable design — remains targeted for 2029.

bear_case.title: Capital intensity
bear_case.description: Rocket Lab is still guiding to a $17–23M quarterly adjusted EBITDA loss even after clearing the Iridium stockholder vote, on top of $1.53B of H1 2026 equity raises; AST SpaceMobile just layered a $1.15B dilutive convertible on top of ~$610M of quarterly capex; Stoke Space's Nova Block 2 isn't targeted until 2029.

bear_case.title: Government concentration
bear_case.description: Redwire's NITE STAR win is one of 15 vendors on a contract with zero guaranteed revenue — the same pattern as the SDA's $3.5B Tranche 3 tracking-layer award, split four ways across Lockheed, L3Harris, Rocket Lab and Northrop Grumman; no single company captures an outsized edge even as Golden Dome spending accelerates.

bear_case.title: SpaceX absorbs the value / sector repricing
bear_case.description: A dominant incumbent with a ~$17B-run-rate Starlink and launch-cost leverage keeps compressing everyone else's margins, and SPCX itself still trades ~26% below its post-IPO high; Redwire's record backlog didn't stop a fresh $1.15B insider-selling disclosure, another sign of the gap between operating results and price across the sector.

bear_case.title: Binary mission risk
bear_case.description: Starship Flight 14 — the first true orbital attempt — flies today after three prior slips in three weeks; Neutron's pad delivery is on track for Q4 2026 but its maiden launch is still exposed to slipping into 2027; Blue Origin's New Glenn return-to-flight timeline remains unconfirmed after tracing its last anomaly to an engine issue.

etfs.name: Procure Space
etfs.summary: Pure-play, revenue-weighted (RKLB, PL, ASTS among top holdings); up roughly 23% over the trailing 12 months as Rocket Lab's Iridium progress offsets Redwire's and AST's rougher weeks.

etfs.name: ARK Space Exploration
etfs.summary: Actively managed with broader tech adjacency; up roughly 18% over the trailing 12 months, continuing to lag the pure-play index funds.

etfs.name: SPDR Kensho Final Frontiers
etfs.summary: Equal-weight, space + defense + deep-sea blend; up roughly 42% over the trailing 12 months, the strongest of the three, helped by defense-adjacent names like L3Harris despite its own share-price weakness.

stance.basis: Weights are a share of a hypothetical 100% sleeve for THIS SECTOR only — not a share of your portfolio. Core and Speculative names carry the weight; Watch and Avoid deliberately carry 0% because the point of those groups is that you are not holding them yet.

positions.name: Rocket Lab
positions.note: Iridium stockholders approved the merger Sept 24 (99.6% of votes, ~81% of shares) — clearing the last major deal-completion risk beyond a still-pending FCC review, with closing now guided to mid-2027 — while Neutron's pad delivery stays on track for Q4 2026; raising weight as the vote meaningfully de-risks the deal even though RKLB remains well off its 52-week high.

positions.name: L3Harris
positions.note: The $4.7B PAC-3 propulsion award and Space & Mission Systems revenue tracking past $13B in 2026 keep the fundamentals intact, but shares are still stuck near 52-week lows with the Kubasik-era securities probe unresolved — holding weight steady until the market credits the backlog. Also sits in the Defense sleeve — don't double-count exposure.

positions.name: AST SpaceMobile
positions.note: 13 BlueBirds are now in orbit on a $1.30B contracted backlog and 60+ MNO partners, but Q2 revenue of $31.5M missed by ~8% on a $125.9M BB7 launch-incident charge and a fresh $1.15B convertible raise adds dilution — holding size steady as commercial proof points and cash burn keep offsetting each other.

positions.name: Intuitive Machines
positions.note: The SXM-11 handover and a record $1.8B backlog kept shares rising (+3% Sept 24) on fresh contract and upgrade momentum, but net insider selling remains heavy at roughly $259M over 12 months — keeping this small until backlog conversion into revenue is clearer.

positions.name: Planet Labs
positions.note: Planet's first profitable quarter is now followed by a Berlin facility to scale Pelican production and a 5.8% rally on the Google Project Suncatcher tailwind; adding a small position as the turnaround gains real evidence, though a co-founder's ~$1.8M sale this week and tightening SpaceX rideshare capacity by 2028 keep it speculative rather than core.

positions.name: Redwire
positions.note: Redwire's NITE STAR win adds one of 15 slots on a Space Force IDIQ with an over-$980M ceiling but zero guaranteed revenue, and doesn't resolve the $1.15B of net insider selling disclosed against a roughly $1B market cap — cutting to Watch until that selling pattern is explained despite the record ~$542M backlog.

positions.name: SpaceX
positions.note: Starlink's ~$17B annualized run-rate keeps growing, but shares still sit roughly 26% below their post-IPO high and Starship Flight 14 — the first true orbital attempt — only flies today after three prior slips; staying on Watch until the launch cadence proves out. UK investors wanting SpaceX exposure without chasing the US listing can get indirect access via Scottish Mortgage (SMT, covered on the Baillie Gifford page).

positions.name: Iridium Communications
positions.note: Rocket Lab's shareholders have now approved the merger (99.6% of votes Sept 24), leaving only FCC review before a mid-2027 close, but the exchange-ratio economics are unchanged and RKLB stock remains the cleaner way to express the same view — still avoiding the standalone name here.
